selected.title: Dynamic Clicking: Aim Training Crash Course #3
selected.subtitles: subtitles/RiddBTW_dynamic_clicking_crashcourse3.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Dynamic clicking = moving targets requiring reading/selection/LEADING/pattern learning; Floating Heads Timing 400% = flick to where target WILL be + micro-adjust, never wait for target to enter crosshair.

selected.title: Dynamic Clicking the Squeakquel: Aim Training Crash Course #4
selected.subtitles: subtitles/RiddBTW_dynamic_clicking_squeakquel4.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Nuance: high-level aimers DO wait for targets — but only when map-reading tells them a target will fall into their pre-placed crosshair; novices should actively lead. Edge tracking for AD-spam bots.

selected.title: Speed Matching in Precise Tracking
selected.subtitles: subtitles/MattyOW_speed_matching_precise_tracking.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Speed matching = sync mouse speed to target speed; the mechanism is tension: too little tension = motion lags behind target (the user's 'tracking slow'); too much = jerky overcorrection.

selected.title: Aim at ANY moving target like a PRO - Dynamic Aim Ep.2
selected.subtitles: subtitles/Voltaic_dynamic_aim_ep2.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: OFFICIAL framework: dynamic clicking has exactly 2 approaches — hit confirmation (track briefly then click, the NOVICE approach that should shrink as you improve) and target leading (flick to a predicted point in space, the ADVANCED approach).

selected.title: Reactive Tracking: Aim Training Crash Course #11
selected.subtitles: subtitles/RiddBTW_reactive_tracking_crashcourse11.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Reactive tracking = hardest aim mechanic, requires reading/reactivity/endurance/muscle control; frequent micro-corrections are the defining work.

selected.title: Why you still struggle with moving targets?
selected.subtitles: subtitles/minigodcs_struggle_moving_targets.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Prediction (pre-aim where target will be) vs active reading (real-time micro-adjust); over-reliance on prediction causes stiff micros on evasive targets; for jittery AD-spam targets deliberately UNDER-aim to speed-match instead of over-correcting.

selected.title: HOW TO: MOVING DOTS
selected.subtitles: subtitles/christmasiscancelled_moving_dots.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Core skill = decide WHEN the bot is safest to hit; hit Bounce180 bots at the apex (slowest, most predictable point), keep crosshair at apex height so only horizontal movement is needed.

selected.title: HOW TO: Thin Gauntlet
selected.subtitles: subtitles/christmasiscancelled_thin_gauntlet.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Isolate weak bots (Thin Gauntlet 357-357, invincible versions); external focus (target/hit-sounds) beats internal focus (wrist mechanics) — internal focus is why micro-adjustment feels awkward/stiff.

selected.title: How to Fix Shaky/Jittery Aim
selected.subtitles: subtitles/Kovaaks_fix_shaky_jittery_aim.en.vtt (auto en)

selected.title: Efficiently Fix Microadjusting [Permanently]
selected.subtitles: subtitles/4Banger_fix_microadjusting.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Micro-adjustment is usually NOT a micro problem — flicks are bad at core; train speed + big targets so the flick-then-adjust chain speeds up; evasive side-to-side bots make micro-adjustment automatic.

selected.title: FIX Your Horrible OVERFLICKING
selected.subtitles: subtitles/4Banger_fix_overflicking.en.vtt (auto en)
selected.core_point: Over-flicking comes from over-correcting after undershooting; under-aim deliberately and micro-correct onto target.
